headline: Recovery week continues with easy-run HR sitting well below the prior period as the +51% block settles.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The lightest days of the block are behind you now, and the picture is consistent: comparable-effort easy runs are landing at a lower heart rate than the prior period, which is exactly what you'd want to see after a four-week block that added half again as much volume. That combination — more work absorbed, lower cost per kilometre — is the signal that the base is genuinely consolidating rather than just accumulating.

Strength frequency has more than doubled versus the prior block and the running streak sits at its all-time high, so nothing here suggests you're giving anything back during the lighter days. This is a recovery week doing its job, not a step down in preparedness. With St. Olavsleden about four weeks out, the aerobic side looks well-positioned; the untrained variable remains the pack carry and sustained climbing rather than fitness itself.
watch_items: Whether weighted-pack running enters the schedule while there's still runway to adapt the carry demand before the event.
Whether ascent per run starts trending toward sustained climbing rather than the rolling profiles logged so far.
Whether the lower easy-run HR holds once volume steps back up, confirming the efficiency gain rather than a recovery-week artefact.
Whether the short nights after hard days start clustering as the event nears.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 190 km vs 126 km prior block (+51%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 153 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 8 runs)
▲ Zone 2: 444 min vs 180-240 min/week target (246% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 5.2%
